spans.s:
Potṛ is the name of one of the priests (Ṛtvij) of the sacri-
ficial ritual. Already known to the Rigveda,^1 he is frequently
mentioned later in the Brāhmaṇas.^2 But as Oldenberg^3
observes, the Potṛ is not in the later literature a priest of any
importance, but is practically a mere name. Judging by the
derivation of the name from the root pū, ‘purify,’ it would
seem that he was properly engaged in the purification of the
Soma pavamāna, ‘Soma purifying itself,’ and was perhaps
employed to sing hymns to this Soma. Potra^4 denotes both
the office and the Soma vessel of the Potṛ.^5
1) i. 94, 6; ii. 5, 2; iv. 9, 3; vii. 16, 5;
ix. 67, 22.
2) Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, vi. 10 et seq.;
Satapatha Brāhmaṇa, iv. 3, 4, 22;
v. 4, 5, 22; xii. 1, 1, 8, etc.
3) Religien des Veda, 383, 391, 395.
4) Rv. ii. 1, 2, and probably i. 76, 4,
though the St. Petersburg Dictionary,
s.v., gives this as an example of the
second use.
5) Rv. i. 15, 2; ii. 36, 2; 37, 2. 4.
